title: Generating sections of an invertible module: the fibre criterion
statement: Let $Y$ be a scheme, $\mathcal L$ an invertible $\mathcal O_Y$-module [def-sc-invertible-module] and $s_0,\dots,s_n\in\Gamma(Y,\mathcal L)$. For $s\in\Gamma(Y,\mathcal L)$ put $Y_s=\{y\in Y:\ s_y\notin\mathfrak m_y\mathcal L_y\}$, i.e. the set of $y$ where the image $s(y)$ of $s$ in $\mathcal L_y\otimes_{\mathcal O_{Y,y}}\kappa(y)$ is nonzero. Then $s_0,\dots,s_n$ generate $\mathcal L$ [def-weil-pbc-generating-sections] if and only if for every $y\in Y$ some $s_i(y)\neq0$, that is, if and only if $Y=Y_{s_0}\cup\dots\cup Y_{s_n}$.

proof.text: Apply generating_sections_iff_stalk_span to the finite family of sections. It identifies Epi of the freeHomEquiv morphism with the pointwise top-span equalities.
At each y obtain a linear equivalence L_y ≃ O_{Y,y} from invertible_stalk_linearEquiv.

For a rank-one module over a local ring, transport maximalIdeal times top along the linear equivalence to the maximal ideal. If every vector lies there, its span does too, so it cannot be top since 1 is outside the maximal ideal. If a vector lies outside, its coordinate is a unit; every element is a scalar multiple of it, explicitly with coefficient e(x) times the inverse unit. Hence the span is top iff some vector lies outside maximalIdeal times top. This is the proved private rankOne_span_iff; no Nakayama or residue-field quotient is needed.
Unfold the nonvanishing predicate, combine the equivalences under forall, and use Set.eq_univ_iff_forall and Set.mem_iUnion to convert the pointwise existence into the union equality.

split_report.summary: Split into six steps: (1) generation (Stacks 01AM, surjectivity in the sense 007U(5)) is equivalent to surjectivity of sigma on all Zariski stalks, by the new Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-locally-surjective-iff-stalks (sheaves on a topological space, TopCat.Presheaf.locally_surjective_iff_surjective_on_stalks; not the etale-site nodes); (2) the image of sigma_y is the O_{Y,y}-span of the germs s_{i,y} (elementary); (3) L_y is free of rank one, so L_y/m_yL_y = L_y (x) kappa(y) is one-dimensional (elementary from def-sc-invertible-module and def-weil-residue-field); (4) Nakayama, the new Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-local-generators (Stacks 00DV (4), IsLocalRing.map_mkQ_eq_top); (5) vectors span a one-dimensional space iff one is nonzero (elementary); (6) conclusion. Statement kept; def-weil-residue-field added to stmt_deps (the statement uses kappa(y) and m_y). lem-weil-pbc-nonvanishing-section-trivializes (01CY: X_s open, trivialization) is not needed and not cited.
